DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 44 s. 2021 16 March 2021 DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGENIERO OIC, DILG-REGION vl (Western Visayas) 6 Pepita Aquino St., Fort San Pedro Iloilo City Dear Dir. Ingeniero: This has reference to your Memorandum dated 27 November 2020, requesting for clarification and guidance in connection with the issuance of EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 187, S. 2020 of the City of Iloilo entitled: AN EXECUTIVE ORDER PROHIBITING THE OPERATIONS OF BEERHOUSES, KARAOKE BARS, AND OTHER SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS WHOSE PRIMARY BUSINESS IS THE SERVING OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES AND PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR ESTABLISHMENTS WHOSE BUSINESS INCLUDE THE SERVING OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES. At the outset, we would like to stress that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it has no authority to declare any issuance by the Local Chief Executive in violation of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC) or other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action. For this reason, we Sha!! discuss only the provisions of law or rules which we deem applicable based on the representations in the letter. Section 455 (b)(2) (iii) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 reads: "SECTION. 455. Chief Executive; Powers, Duties and Compensation. - xxxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the city mayor shall: xxx

(2) Enforce all laws and ordinances relative to the governance of the city and in the exercise of the appropriate corporate powers provided for under section 22 of this Code, implement all approved policies, programs, projects, services and activities of the city and, in addition to the foregoing, shall: (iii) Issue such executive orders for the faithful and appropriate enforcement and execution of laws and ordinances;" Based on the foregoing, the City Mayor is authorized to issue an executive order for the faithfui and appropriate enforcement and execution of laws and ordinances. Upon perusal of the aforesaid EO, it appears that the same was issued pursuant to Section 16 of the Local Government Code of 1991 in relation to the declaration of a State of Calamity by the President due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In the case of Manila Public School Teachers' Association (MPSTA) v. Mr. Winston F. Garcia, et al. (G.R. No. 192708, October 2, 2017), the Supreme Court made a pronouncement explaining that when an executive order or any administrative issuance for that matter "substantially affects the rights of those govemed", then publication is indispensable. The High Court further emphasized that "when xxx an administrative rule goes beyond merely providing for the means that can facilitate or render least cumbersome the implementation of the law but substantially adds to or increases the burden of those governed, it behooves the agency to accord at least to those directly affected a chance to be heard, and thereafter to be duly informed, before that new issuance is given the force and effect of law. " Thus, interpretative regulations that do not add anything to the law or affect substantial rights of any person do not entail publication. This is because 'they give no real consequence more than what the law itself has already prescribed' q, and administrative rules and regulations wherein the purpose is to enforce or implement an existing law publication is a condition precedent for its validity, bearing in mind that the reason for the indispensability of publication is to ensure the constitutional right to due process. I Association of Southern Tagalog Electric Cooperatives. Inc. v. Energy Regulatory Commission, 695 Phil. 243(2012) further citing CIP v. CA, 329 Phil. 987 (1996)

Lastly, pursuant to Section 455 (b)(l )(xii) of the Local Government Code, copies of the executive orders issued by HUC Mayors are required to be furnished to the Office of the President within seventy-two (72) hours after its issuance. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, y the thority of the Secretary: MA GAN, CESO Ill cer-• -Charge Office of the Undersecretary for Local Government Ls/32/17
